subject: Audit evidence provenance & export scaling for admin events — Helix Therapeutics request
messages:
From: Amy Carter <amy.carter@helixtx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin-events evidence provenance + large export options

Hi Marissa,

We're kicking off our SOC 2 scope review and need a clear description of what Redwood records for 'admin events' (we'll provide the exact control mapping later). For the auditor we need to validate:

- fields captured (actor id, actor role, action, resource id, before/after state, request id, API key id, source IP, user agent, timestamp with timezone)
- whether we include raw request/response payloads or just metadata
- retention windows by event class and how to apply legal/regulatory carveouts
- export formats you support (Parquet/JSONL/CSV), manifest/checksum process for integrity, and signing model
- options for scrubbing PII and what you can pseudonymize vs fully redact
- chain-of-custody (signed manifests, HMAC, time-ordered slices)
- delivery choices (SFTP, presigned S3, GS, SFTP with PGP) and the required credentials/provisioning flow

Scale note: our security team expects ~6 months of admin event data (~3.8 TB compressed estimate) across two regions. Please outline throughput and ETA for a one-time full export plus an incremental/daily option.

Can you send a short doc and a sample manifest the auditors can examine? We're on a tight schedule — auditor kickoff is 2026-09-02.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Carter
Director, Security Operations
Helix Therapeutics

Hi Amy,

Thanks for the clear ask — we can provide the detail the auditor needs. High-level items below; I'll attach a short spec and a sample manifest in my next note.

What we log (admin events):
- actor: internal user id (uid), role, service account id / API key id
- action: canonical action name (e.g., iam.user.update), resource type/id, request id, operation outcome (success/fail)
- context: source IP, user agent, region, request duration, correlated trace id when available
- before/after deltas for config changes (we keep a compressed JSON diff)
- timestamp: UTC with RFC3339 timestamp and original timezone metadata
- retention label: admin-critical | privileged-change | operator-access (configurable per account)

Export options and integrity:
- formats: JSONL (line-delimited JSON) and Parquet (partitioned by date and region). CSV available for small slices.
- delivery: presigned S3 (recommended), GCS signed URL, or SFTP over FTPS with PGP payload option.
- integrity: per-file SHA256 checksums plus a signed manifest file. Manifests are signed with our KMS-backed signing key and include a per-slice sequence number and event range.
- chain-of-custody: manifest contains creation timestamp, operator id, delivery URI, file checksums, and a cumulative HMAC. We can provide the public verification key for audits.

Privacy and redaction:
- by default we do not export full request bodies unless explicitly requested. For payloads we can provide pseudonymization: replace direct PII fields with stable pseudonyms and keep a sealed mapping when required for legal processes.

Scale and ETA:
- full export of ~4 TB compressed: baseline job estimated 36-72 hours (depends on regional egress and chosen delivery).
- incremental mode: daily snapshots (slice per UTC day) delivered to a presigned bucket within 24 hours of slice close.

I'll loop in our infra lead (kimberly) and engineering (Neha) to confirm partitioning, throttles, and exact timelines. After we agree on redaction and delivery mode we'll produce a sample manifest and an export_spec_v1.pdf.

Action items:
1) Amy: confirm you want payloads pseudonymized or fully redacted.
2) Amy: confirm preferred delivery (S3 presigned recommended).
3) Marissa/Kimberly/Neha: produce sample manifest + spec.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi all,

Quick technical clarifications from infra that affect ETA and integrity:

- Partitioning: we'll slice by UTC date + region + event_class. This keeps Parquet file sizes sane for parallel download.
- Order guarantees: each slice will come with a min/max event_id and timestamps; within-slice order is preserved but slices are not globally ordered — the manifest provides event ranges so auditors can reconstruct chronological order.
- Delta vs full: we can provide a full historical dump or a delta-only mode (deltas keep prior-state references). For forensic needs we recommend full dumps plus daily deltas for incremental verification.
- Manifest signing: we use KMS to sign the manifest (RSA-PSS) and include both the signature and signer fingerprint. We can also provide a detached signature (sig file).
- Transport: presigned S3 is fastest. For SFTP we'll do mutually-agreed keys and rotate them post-delivery.

We'll need Neha to confirm resource scaling and whether we can meet a 36-hour SLA for a 4 TB job in us-west-2 without impacting prod.

-Kimberly
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: admin-events evidence provenance + large export options

Hi team,

Implementation notes from engineering:

- Throttling & contended windows: we'll schedule a dedicated export job in an isolated export cluster to avoid production impact. For a ~3.8 TB compressed export I estimate ~30-50 GiB/s read throughput and network egress dependence; net wall time ~24-60 hrs depending on egress throttles and whether we perform server-side compression during streaming.
- File layout: NDJSON shards (target ~512 MB compressed) + Parquet for analytic slices. Each shard gets a SHA256, and the manifest includes cumulative event count and min/max timestamps.
- Checksum strategy: per-file SHA256 + manifest SHA256; manifest signed with KMS and an HMAC field for quick verification by auditors. We'll also produce a small attestation doc with the signing key fingerprint.
- PII scrubbing: two modes — pseudonymize (stable tokenization) or redact (remove fields). Pseudonymization uses a per-customer salt stored in a sealed KMS envelope; if Helix wants mapping unlocked we require an authorized legal request.
- Timezone normalization: we store UTC primary; original timezone is recorded as metadata per event. Auditor-friendly exports will include both.

Delivery modes and ETAs:
1) Bulk one-time export to presigned S3 bucket: ~36-48 hours end-to-end if Helix provides the destination bucket and accepts presigned uploads. This includes checksum generation and manifest signing.
2) Incremental daily slices: available within 18-24 hours of slice close. Ideal if you want continuous access and easier validation.

Attachments: sample_manifest.json (attached) — contains a representative manifest with file checksums, sequence numbers, and a signer field.

I'll schedule a dry run on a small window (72 hours) to validate throughput and the manifest signing flow.

-Neha
Senior Software Engineer, Infra
